newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada poll shows Bloc inching ahead in Quebec.
newsitem.headline: Canada poll shows Bloc inching ahead in Quebec.

text.p: The separatist Bloc Quebecois has inched ahead of Canada's ruling Liberal Party in Quebec as Canadians prepare to vote in a federal election on June 2, a poll released on Friday showed.

The Leger and Leger poll, commissioned by Toronto's Globe and Mail and the Journal de Montreal, put the Bloc at 36.1 percent, with the Liberals at 34.6 percent and the Conservatives at 26.3 percent among decided voters.
The poll surveyed 1,005 eligibile voters from Monday to Wednesday this week. Results are considered accurate 19 times out of 20 with a margin of error of 3.1 percentage points.
A similar Leger and Leger poll a week earlier found that 34 percent of decided voters supported the Liberals, with 33 percent for the Bloc and 31 percent for the Conservatives.
Much of the Liberal support was concentrated in Montreal, giving the Bloc a good chance at winning seats outside Montreal, the Globe and Mail reported.
The poll found about 14 percent of voters were undecided.

The Bloc was the official opposition in the last parliament. Nationally, it faces a challenge for official opposition status from the right-wing Reform Party, whose strength is based in the western provinces.
Under Canadian electoral law, Friday is the last day polls can be reported before the election.
